headline: Oil spike and hawkish Fed bets pull markets into risk-off mode
body: Tuesday's session set a risk-off tone that's carried into Wednesday: the Dow fell 1.2% while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq slipped 0.6% and 0.3% as traders returned from the long weekend to renewed Middle East escalation — US strikes on Iranian tankers near Kharg Island pushed Brent crude toward $99 and WTI near $94. Futures were only modestly lower into Wednesday's open, but the oil move matters beyond energy: it's feeding a market now pricing roughly 60% odds of a rate hike, not a cut, at next week's FOMC meeting, with Treasury yields near three-year highs. Layer on fresh US-Canada trade friction — a new ban on Canadian motorcycle imports — and Friday's CPI print looks like the week's real catalyst.

Retail chatter today reads more stock-specific than macro-directional. StockTwits and Reddit threads are buzzing around names like IREN, on a data-center power grid approval fueling short-squeeze talk, and Solaris Energy after an EBITDA-outlook raise, while McDonald's trading near 52-week lows and Lyft's mixed quarter are splitting community sentiment between value and value-trap framing. None of that amounts to a coordinated bullish or bearish tilt on the broader tape — it's idiosyncratic story-stock activity layered on a cautious macro backdrop. The more telling risk-off signal sits in adjacent assets: bitcoin slipping below $80,000 earlier this week suggests speculative appetite is retreating alongside equities rather than offering a risk-on offset.
